title: When the Hollow Burns Anew
premise: Wren Eriksen has spent ten years guarding the Hollow Gate, a sealed passage between the human realm of Thornfell and the fading fae country of Vaelmoor, bound by a covenant that keeps both worlds alive but apart. When the crown declares a purge of anyone bearing the old gift, Wren's hidden magic marks her as prey, and she flees into the mountains with a ragged band of fugitives who slowly become the family she never had. To survive, she must reopen the gate and reforge the shattered covenant between realms, but the truth she uncovers—that the crown's hunt is a cover for a noble house draining Vaelmoor's magic to sustain itself—means exposing the very kingdom that raised her. In the end, Wren sacrifices her own gift to bind the new covenant, choosing loyalty to her found family and both worlds over the comfortable lies of the old one, and the gate burns open at last.
about_author: Mara Pemberton is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade drawing mountain passes before turning to fiction about the things that hide in them. She writes from a drafty farmhouse where the wind, she insists, occasionally answers back.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Watch
chapters.summary: Wren Eriksen patrols the sealed Hollow Gate, hiding her small gift from even her closest friend, the smuggler Doss. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness beneath routine competence, and the first crack—her magic flaring when she touches the gate's cold stone.

chapters.title: Proclamation in Ashford
chapters.summary: In the market town of Ashford, criers announce the crown's hunt for the gifted. Wren watches a neighbor dragged away and realizes her name is on a list she cannot see. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: fear curdling into the decision to run before the soldiers reach the mountains.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Roads
chapters.summary: Wren uses her secret knowledge of the Thornfell passes to flee, but Doss betrays her location to buy his own pardon. She escapes his ambush with the help of a strange, half-starved fugitive boy named Callum. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: betrayal's sting, and the first reluctant bond.

chapters.title: The Fugitives of Greyfen
chapters.summary: Wren reaches the hidden camp of Greyfen, where the gifted hide under the fierce leadership of Sera Voss, a disgraced royal guard. They distrust Wren's gatekeeper past. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: suspicion versus necessity—Wren is the only one who knows the mountain roads.

chapters.title: What the Boy Carried
chapters.summary: Callum's secret emerges: he carries a shard of the old covenant stone, which sings when Wren is near. Sera realizes Wren is not just a keeper but a potential reforging hand. POV: Callum. Emotional beat: wonder and terror as the boy's burden becomes everyone's hope.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Crown hunters led by the cold, gifted-turned-traitor Aldric Kane assault Greyfen. The camp burns; Sera's people scatter into the high passes. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: grief and fury, and Sera's grudging decision that Wren is now their best weapon.

chapters.title: Into the Deep Passes
chapters.summary: The fugitives cross the frozen high passes, and Wren teaches them her smuggler's tricks. Callum collapses from the shard's drain, and Wren's gift, used openly for the first time, saves him. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the camp's fear of her transforms into trust.

chapters.title: The Court of Cinders
chapters.summary: In the capital, Lord Halloway of the crown's inner circle oversees the hunt, revealing to Kane that the gifted are being harvested to feed a dying Vaelmoor. POV: Kane. Emotional beat: Kane's first doubt as he sees what the 'hunt' truly is.

chapters.title: The Other Side of the Stone
chapters.summary: The fugitives reach a forgotten waygate where the shard resonates. Through it, Wren glimpses Vaelmoor: a beautiful realm dimming toward death. A fae envoy, Ilyen, slips through and begs their help. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: awe and guilt—the covenant's collapse is killing a whole world.

chapters.title: Terms of the Broken
chapters.summary: Ilyen explains the old covenant: a reforging requires a keeper's hand, a shard, and a truth spoken at the Hollow Gate. But the truth demanded may destroy whoever speaks it. Sera and Wren argue over the cost. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: loyalty strained against the price of truth.

chapters.title: Doss's Debt
chapters.summary: Doss, guilt-ridden, finds them and offers the soldiers' route schedules as penance. Sera wants him hanged; Wren argues mercy. POV: Doss. Emotional beat: shame and the fragile arithmetic of forgiveness within a found family.

chapters.title: The Harvest Fields
chapters.summary: The group raids a crown facility and discovers cages of harvested gifted, their magic piped through Halloway's machines toward the mountains. Among the freed prisoners is Wren's childhood mentor, dying. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: righteous rage hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Kane's Choice
chapters.summary: Kane intercepts the freed prisoners but, confronted with the harvested children, lets them go and turns his evidence toward Halloway. Halloway's men mark him for death. POV: Kane. Emotional beat: a traitor's painful turn toward conscience.

chapters.title: Winter Camp
chapters.summary: Snowbound in a shepherd's bothy, the fugitives share their stories—Sera's disgrace, Callum's orphaning, Wren's years of hiding. For one night they are simply people, not fugitives. POV: Callum. Emotional beat: the found family crystallizes; Callum finally feels he belongs.

chapters.title: The Road to Hollow Gate
chapters.summary: The group makes for the Hollow Gate, but Halloway has moved the harvest operation there itself, intending to drain the gate's last magic and seal Vaelmoor's fate forever. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: dread—the place of her duty has become the enemy's stronghold.

chapters.title: The Truth Wren Buried
chapters.summary: Wren confesses to Sera: ten years ago she helped seal the gate, believing she was saving Thornfell from a fae war, and her sealing began Vaelmoor's decline. Sera's trust shatters. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the theme's crux—truth offered too late, loyalty hanging by a thread.

chapters.title: Storming the Hollow
chapters.summary: The assault on the gate begins. Doss dies holding the smuggler's tunnel open so the others can pass; Kane arrives, wounded, with proof of Halloway's crimes. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: sacrifice and grief braided with momentum toward the climax.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: At the gate's heart, Wren faces Halloway and the harvest engine. She begins the reforging, but the rite demands a truth spoken—and hers is the heaviest. Callum's shard blazes; the covenant stone reforms in her hands. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose at the story's climax.

chapters.title: What the Gate Demanded
chapters.summary: To complete the covenant, Wren surrenders her own gift into the stone—the last price. Halloway falls, consumed by the magic his machines stole returning to its source. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: loss and transcendence; she gives up the thing that made her hunted and made her herself.

chapters.title: Two Worlds, One Threshold
chapters.summary: The gate reopens as a bridge, not a barrier. Ilyen's people cross to trade and heal; Thornfell's king, confronted with Kane's evidence, rescinds the hunt. Sera and Wren reconcile—loyalty rebuilt on truth rather than silence. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: reconciliation and the dawning of a new order.

chapters.title: The Keeper No More
chapters.summary: Wren, giftless, is offered her old post and refuses. Instead she founds a school at the gate for children of both realms, with Callum as her first student and Sera as its shield. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not assigned; the family made permanent.

chapters.title: When the Hollow Burns Anew
chapters.summary: A year later, the gate burns with festival light on both sides of the mountains. Wren, watching Callum teach younger children, feels the old hollow in her filled at last. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet, earned joy—the closing echo of the title and the story's heart.
